use_when.text: Use it for actions that are clear from the icon alone, such as notifications.
Use Primary for the one main icon action in a group.
Use Outline when it sits on its own, such as next to the Avatar.
Use Ghost inside toolbars, cards and the Sidebar.
Turn on Show badge when there is something new.

dont_use_when.text: Do not use it for actions people may not recognise from the icon. Use Button with a label.
Do not use it for the main action on a screen.
Do not put a number in the badge.
Do not change the icon colour, except on static surfaces such as the Sidebar.
Do not recolour it outside the bound tokens.

best_practice.text: Show the action’s name as a tooltip on hover.
Use the same icon for the same action everywhere.

variant_intent.intent: Use Primary for the one main icon action in a group.
Use Outline when it sits on its own, such as next to the Avatar.
Use Ghost inside toolbars, cards and the Sidebar.

placement.text: Sidebar header, Style Ghost, as the collapse/expand toggle with icon menu (expanded) or maximize (collapsed).

pairs_with.how: Default bell Icon at Size md, replaceable through the "Icon swap" slot

a11y.text: Renders a native <button> with type="button" by default.
aria-label is a required prop and is the only accessible name; the icon wrapper is aria-hidden="true".
The badge dot is aria-hidden="true"; the prop comment says to include the badge in the aria-label, such as "Notifications, 3 unread".
State Disabled sets the native disabled attribute.
Give it an aria-label, such as "Notifications". The icon alone is not a name.
Include the badge in the name, such as "Notifications, 3 unread".
Keep a visible focus indicator on keyboard focus (:focus-visible).
Icons are above 3:1 in every enabled style.

gaps.detail: State=Default, Hover, Disabled: the Figma documentation page for Icon Button (205:109) does not say what these values are for (checked usage region 205:452).
